cohort: 370 women with singleton gestation, no medical or psychological problems during pregnancy, and an Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) score <13 during pregnancy
finding: Emergency caesarean section was associated with a higher risk of postpartum depression at 8 and 16 weeks postpartum compared to elective caesarean section and normal vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Emergency caesarean section showed a stronger correlation with postpartum depression than elective caesarean section.
